one_line: A browser-native spreadsheet exposing structured, stateful editing tools to an agent.
what_it_does: Lets a person and agent share a live workbook, with formula recalculation, structured edits, range operations, formatting, notes, and undo.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes the live in-memory workbook and dependency-aware operations with changed-cell results, shared cursor/focus, and concurrent human edits; generic UI driving would be materially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: IronCalc runs in-browser with no server-side workbook copy.
Writes return recalculation ripple and changed cells.
Person and agent operate on the same editable workbook state.
execution_rationale: The packet and frame sheet show a coherent conversational-to-spreadsheet workflow and a visible grid artifact, but no submitted video or end-to-end tool invocation evidence limits claimed completeness.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and public repository exists.
Frame sheet shows prompt, assistant response, loading state, and spreadsheet artifact.
Description specifies twelve workbook operations.
impact_rationale: Spreadsheet users and model builders have a concrete need for reliable formula-preserving collaboration; the product directly addresses transcription, dependency, and synchronization errors.
impact_evidence: Stable cell addresses and dependency graph are central to the stated workflow.
Human edits are incorporated into subsequent agent results.
creativity_rationale: Treating the spreadsheet as a shared agent-human computational workspace, rather than a generated export, is a fresh and well-articulated interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Shared editable intermediate state is emphasized.
Agent focus and annotations are represented in the sheet.
usability_note: The visible spreadsheet workflow appears understandable, though actual agent controls are not demonstrated in submitted video.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame evidence appears to show artifact generation but not WebMCP calls.
standouts: Structured recalculation feedback and shared live workbook state.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP delta and credible productivity use case; advance despite limited direct invocation evidence.

one_line: An SDK and UI rig that makes invisible WebMCP agent activity visible to humans.
what_it_does: Provides connection status, onboarding, live work states, history, permission prompts, and deeplinked side-by-side human-agent sessions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP supplies the event and tool surface that Dolly visualizes, improving shared-state observability and permission UX, though a general agent plus application instrumentation could reproduce much of it.
leverage_evidence: SDK follows agent actions and exposes connection, work, history, and permission states.
One-click Open in ChatGPT starts a paired session.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent SDK concept covering the full multiplayer session arc and gallery evidence exists, but no video or direct runnable workflow evidence is supplied.
execution_evidence: Ten gallery images are reported.
Description enumerates onboarding, connection, work, history, and permission surfaces.
Public repository and alive demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Developers building agent-enabled interfaces have a real need to communicate invisible automation and preserve human control; value is credible but SDK adoption is not demonstrated.
impact_evidence: Targets a recurring usability gap: invisible tool calls provide no progress or outcome visibility.
Reusable React SDK is the stated delivery model.
creativity_rationale: The camera-rig metaphor and explicit co-op multiplayer framing are a notably fresh interaction model for agent UX.
creativity_evidence: Treats agent activity as something the interface should keep in frame.
Full session arc is designed as multiplayer UX.
usability_note: Status and permission surfaces should improve trust, though live behavior is not directly evidenced.
red_flags: No submitted video; claims are primarily packaging and description based.
standouts: Strong framing of agent actions as visible multiplayer state.
Reusable SDK rather than one-off demo.
advance_reason: Distinctive, relevant infrastructure/UX concept with credible scope and impact.

one_line: A structured accessibility directory agents can search without guessing from generic labels.
what_it_does: Collects detailed observations about entrances, doors, parking, routes, restrooms, seating, counters, elevators, and supports agent search and updates.
leverage_rationale: Structured, uncertainty-aware accessibility records are substantially more precise for agent filtering and comparison than UI scraping, especially when the correct answer is unknown.
leverage_evidence: Ten explicit accessibility categories are represented.
Project emphasizes returning unknown rather than guessing.
Agents search and compare structured observations.
execution_rationale: The existing platform plus described WebMCP extension is coherent, but the packet provides no video and only limited direct evidence of the new agent workflow.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and repository public.
Description clearly distinguishes pre-existing platform from challenge extension.
impact_rationale: People with mobility and access needs face a concrete, high-stakes information gap; detailed, current, uncertainty-honest place data can directly improve trip decisions.
impact_evidence: Addresses steps, doors, parking, interior routes, and other practical barriers.
Explicitly avoids unsupported accessibility claims.
creativity_rationale: The concept is not wholly novel, but the structured observation model and agent-mediated accessibility planning are a strong, socially meaningful synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Agent access is built around granular access requirements rather than a binary label.
Community evidence and agent upkeep are combined.
usability_note: Requirement-based search could be highly useful; actual interaction quality is not evidenced.
red_flags: Pre-existing product; challenge contribution is described but not visibly demonstrated.
standouts: High-stakes audience fit and explicit uncertainty discipline.
advance_reason: Exceptional audience need and meaningful structured-data leverage outweigh thin execution evidence.

one_line: A shared browser chessboard where human and agent take validated turns with coaching.
what_it_does: Supports human or agent play, board-state inspection, legal moves, waiting, Stockfish analysis, move evaluation, and adjustable agent strength.
leverage_rationale: Chess is stateful and turn-based; typed board state and legal move tools let the agent act reliably on the same validated game state without DOM interpretation.
leverage_evidence: Eight page-registered tools cover state, legal moves, turns, and analysis.
Human and agent share one board and move history.
Analysis outputs structured from/to/promotion fields.
execution_rationale: The described core loop is coherent and includes validation and coaching, but the submitted video predates engine work and no video is supplied in this packet beyond frame references.
execution_evidence: Demo alive, public repo, and four gallery images reported.
Description distinguishes the five-tool video from the current eight-tool app.
Live claims include legal move validation and Stockfish coaching.
impact_rationale: Chess learners and players gain a credible practice/coaching experience, especially through move explanations and beatable agent strength.
impact_evidence: Move evaluation reports centipawn cost, error class, and refutation line.
Engine strength can be weakened without weakening advice.
creativity_rationale: Chess itself is established, but shared human-agent turn-taking plus structured coaching is a fresh and well-targeted WebMCP interaction.
creativity_evidence: Agent can be handed control mid-game.
Wait-for-human-move creates a genuine alternating workflow.
usability_note: Familiar board plus explicit coaching likely supports approachable play, though current UI behavior is not directly observed.
red_flags: Evidence note says submitted video predates three current engine tools.
standouts: Strong stateful-tool fit and useful structured coaching outputs.
advance_reason: A clear, demonstrable stateful WebMCP use case with meaningful user value.

one_line: A Chicago deals planner where an agent ranks live offers and a person edits the shared night-out plan.
what_it_does: Searches time-sensitive deals and venues, supports nearby and cuisine filters, booking links, community tips, and a shared Tonight plan with human constraints and vetoes.
leverage_rationale: Structured time-windowed inventory and a shared editable plan address the precision and state problems of agent browsing; stale or mislocated offers are materially less likely.
leverage_evidence: 17 tools cover live-corpus searches and Tonight-plan state.
Inventory is described as 80,000+ deals re-verified weekly.
Person controls taste and veto while agent ranks options.
execution_rationale: The product story and five gallery images suggest a substantial flow, but demo status is unknown and no video or direct end-to-end evidence is supplied.
execution_evidence: Five gallery images reported.
Description separates ten data tools and seven plan tools.
Booking links and confirmation-gated write are specified.
impact_rationale: People planning an evening have a concrete discovery and coordination problem; current local deal data plus shared planning can save time and reduce stale recommendations.
impact_evidence: Targets Chicago residents across neighborhoods and suburbs.
Handles day, time, location, cuisine, and booking needs.
creativity_rationale: The explicit division of labor—agent ranking versus human taste and veto—makes ordinary local search into a compelling collaborative planning model.
creativity_evidence: Shared Tonight plan is editable by both parties.
Time-sensitive deal corpus is integrated with collaborative intent.
usability_note: The shared plan and constraints are promising, but unknown demo health reduces confidence.
red_flags: Demo status unknown; no submitted video.
standouts: Strong human/agent division of labor for a real planning task.
advance_reason: High practical value and strong collaborative concept, with execution risk flagged.

one_line: A governed WebMCP control plane for inspecting, repairing, testing, and rolling back a shared game world.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect typed world state, find quest blockers, simulate seeded outcomes, propose and execute approved repairs, validate provenance, and rollback checkpoints.
leverage_rationale: The typed, stateful, approval-gated control plane makes complex live-ops and QA workflows practical and reproducible; generic UI automation cannot comparably provide domain-safe inspection, simulation, repair, and rollback.
leverage_evidence: Thirty browser-native capabilities span inspection, simulation, repair, governance, and rollback.
Closed schemas and stable IDs are described.
Demonstration finds a circular quest dependency, repairs it after approval, validates reachability, then rolls back.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete, internally coherent defect-to-repair-to-regression-to-rollback scenario and an alive demo, though no submitted video limits direct proof.
execution_evidence: Central circular-dependency workflow is specified end to end.
Human approval and provenance are part of the workflow.
Demo reported alive and public repository exists.
impact_rationale: Game teams and live-ops/QA practitioners have a concrete need to diagnose progression failures safely; deterministic simulation and reversible repairs offer credible value.
impact_evidence: Targets inspection, reproduction, balancing, approval, validation, and recovery.
Rollback makes regressions reproducible.
creativity_rationale: A human-governed repair laboratory for interactive worlds is an ambitious and memorable extension of WebMCP beyond ordinary agent actions.
creativity_evidence: Combines game-world control, QA simulation, governance, and reversible repair.
The circular dependency is used as a concrete narrative test case.
usability_note: Approval gates and typed domain actions support safe expert use, though the breadth may be complex for newcomers.
red_flags: No submitted video; high claims rely on packet description.
standouts: Exceptional WebMCP indispensability and safety/governance design.
advance_reason: Most compelling leverage case: structured agent operations materially change what safe game-world QA can do.

one_line: A tool-driven open-source contribution navigator that matches skills to active, available issues.
what_it_does: Stores skills, matches projects, analyzes responsiveness, finds and checks issues, drafts plans, drives graph highlighting, and tracks contributions through merge.
leverage_rationale: Structured chaining over live GitHub data reduces research friction and can update shared UI state, though a general agent with GitHub access could reproduce much of the outcome.
leverage_evidence: Nineteen tools chain matching, responsiveness, issue availability, difficulty, planning, and tracking.
Agent highlighting changes the live skill graph.
Dashboard tracks Interested to Merged.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent path from skills to issue to contribution tracking and has gallery evidence, but no video or direct execution proof.
execution_evidence: Demo alive and public repository reported.
Six gallery images reported.
Workflow includes live GitHub data and persistent dashboard state.
impact_rationale: New contributors face a real discovery and confidence barrier; surfacing available, suitable issues and project responsiveness can credibly increase successful contributions.
impact_evidence: Addresses project selection, issue availability, difficulty, review likelihood, and follow-up.
Targets a common open-source onboarding problem.
creativity_rationale: The concept is a strong synthesis of contribution discovery and agent research, with a memorable live graph interaction but familiar underlying domain.
creativity_evidence: Skill graph reacts to agent actions.
Combines issue matching with response-time evidence and journey tracking.
usability_note: Plain-language goals and progressive contribution tracking are promising; live quality is not directly evidenced.
red_flags: No submitted video; claims about live GitHub data are not independently demonstrated in the packet.
standouts: Useful end-to-end contributor journey and agent-driven graph feedback.
advance_reason: Clear audience/problem fit with meaningful agent research leverage and coherent scope.

one_line: A shared architecture canvas where humans and agents design and inspect structured cloud systems.
what_it_does: Provides a visual architecture workspace with structured actions for creating, modifying, analyzing, improving, and challenging a shared design without external model keys.
leverage_rationale: Structured architecture entities and direct canvas mutations keep diagram and system representation synchronized, avoiding fragile visual manipulation and text-only drift.
leverage_evidence: Agent and human operate on one shared cloud design.
Capabilities are exposed directly from the architecture editor through WebMCP.
No chatbot, LLM API, cloud keys, or credentials required.
execution_rationale: The concept and packaging are coherent and two gallery images exist, but the packet provides no video and its available text does not establish a complete end-to-end workflow.
execution_evidence: Demo alive and public repository reported.
Architecture canvas and structured collaboration are clearly described.
Two gallery images reported.
impact_rationale: Architects and engineering teams have a real synchronization and review problem across chat, diagrams, and decisions; a shared structured canvas could reduce that friction.
impact_evidence: Directly targets fragmented architecture design workflows.
Supports inspection, improvement, and challenge of the same design.
creativity_rationale: The shared visual-system design model is a fresh and ambitious application of WebMCP, especially without requiring a proprietary inference backend.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language reasoning and visual system design share one workspace.
Agent can modify structured architecture rather than generate a static diagram.
usability_note: A canvas plus direct agent collaboration is plausible, but interaction quality is not shown in video evidence.
red_flags: No submitted video; limited visible proof of the collaboration loop.
standouts: No-key architecture copilot and shared structured visual state.
advance_reason: Strong concept and leverage with credible audience value, held back by thin execution evidence.

one_line: An observability, testing, security, and FinOps console for WebMCP applications.
what_it_does: Discovers exposed tools, inspects schemas and traces, runs goal tests, detects regressions and unsafe chains, estimates costs, and supports replay and CI gates.
leverage_rationale: A WebMCP-native introspection and replay surface can expose structured tool behavior more precisely than UI observation; however, the broad platform claims are not demonstrated.
leverage_evidence: Claims automatic discovery of website tools and schema/permission inspection.
AgentCI, security attack graphs, traces, replay, and CI enforcement are described.
ToolTracer itself exposes WebMCP tools.
execution_rationale: The demo is reported dead and no frame sheets or video were submitted; the packet is primarily a large feature description, so claimed completeness cannot be credited strongly.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=dead.
No video frame sheets submitted.
Devpost screenshot is packaging evidence only.
impact_rationale: Teams deploying agent systems have real needs around regression, security, reliability, and cost, but impact remains conditional on the platform actually functioning.
impact_evidence: Targets concrete production concerns: failures, unsafe permissions, latency, and cost.
CI/CD enforcement is a credible intended use.
creativity_rationale: The unified combination of WebMCP observability, goal testing, security attack graphs, and FinOps is ambitious and potentially distinctive.
creativity_evidence: Cross-cuts behavior, security, and cost in one agent trace.
Uses the product to investigate other WebMCP applications.
usability_note: No live demo or product-motion evidence is available, so usability is unclear and likely not ready for assessment.
red_flags: Feature breadth substantially exceeds demonstrated evidence.
advance_reason: Potentially valuable and creative, but dead demo and absent execution evidence fail the stage-1 evidence bar.

one_line: A healthcare price-transparency dashboard exposing claims search, comparison, and provider summaries to agents.
what_it_does: Makes healthcare claims and provider pricing data searchable and comparable through three structured WebMCP capabilities while retaining a human dashboard.
leverage_rationale: Structured search, comparison, and summarization are a real improvement over navigating complex claims interfaces, but the described operations are conventional data queries and only modestly WebMCP-specific.
leverage_evidence: Three explicit capabilities cover searching claims, comparing procedures, and summarizing providers.
Dashboard and agent are intended to use the same underlying claims data.
execution_rationale: The demo is reported alive and two gallery images show the dashboard, but no video and no detailed end-to-end evidence limit confidence in the extension.
execution_evidence: Demo alive and public repository reported.
Two gallery images reported.
Project identifies a prior claims/MRF foundation and a challenge extension.
impact_rationale: Patients, caregivers, and cost-conscious healthcare users have a real problem understanding opaque procedure prices; structured comparisons could provide credible decision support, with appropriate caution.
impact_evidence: Targets difficult-to-search healthcare claims and provider pricing data.
Search, comparison, and summaries map directly to user needs.
creativity_rationale: Agent-ready healthcare pricing is useful and timely, but the concept is a relatively straightforward application of structured search and summarization.
creativity_evidence: Extends an existing healthcare claims application with WebMCP.
Human dashboard and agent access share underlying data.
usability_note: A focused dashboard may be approachable, but no interaction sequence or agent behavior is shown.
red_flags: No submitted video; challenge extension is not directly demonstrated.
Healthcare pricing data quality and interpretation are consequential but not evidenced here.
standouts: Clear practical use case for structured healthcare data.
advance_reason: Credible impact but limited novelty, modest WebMCP delta, and thin evidence make it a weaker advance candidate.
